review.note: Release 0.7.0 makes qualified source bootstrap own each parent initializer's bytes or explicit absence and requires bootstrap before ordinary parent imports. Controller-to-worker authority preserves the existing runtime source, namespace topology, assertion-hook protections and three-item toolkit registration. V2 review evidence independently binds candidate parent Git mode/blob and current mode/hash, including ignored additions, without weakening 0.6.0 process cleanup or diagnostics-before-publication ordering. No application-data migration is needed: regenerate snapshots with sync and run handwritten entries in a fresh process with bootstrap first; arbitrary initializer side effects and import ordering cannot safely be rewritten automatically. Old review evidence requires a new full-repository baseline. All 144 targeted tests passed in 99.03 seconds, including real local workers, accepted stale-bytecode negative controls, parent drift, full baseline invalidation, offline revision verification, checkout portability, managed publication and consumer snapshot merge profiles. Ruff, formatter, strict mypy and Markdown checks passed; formal review and exact-candidate gate still run at integration. Native Windows execution is not claimed by this POSIX run. No dependency bounds, pins or runtime dependencies changed. Fresh PyPI/npm discovery exactly matches the complete already-reviewed 0.6.0 candidate metadata: hatchling 1.32.4, packaging 26.3, build 1.6.1, mypy 2.4.0, pytest 9.1.1, pytest-xdist 3.8.0, ruff 0.17.1 and markdownlint-cli2 0.23.3. All satisfy declared ranges and Python candidates support 3.14. There are no newer candidates since that audit, so its identical upstream release-note conclusions remain applicable, including Ruff 0.17.1 with no preview/PYI/PERF rules enabled. The normally resolved local environment uses Python 3.14.1, command-local uv 0.13.0, these candidates and installed project metadata 0.7.0. This audit records dependency review and does not itself prove final gate or publication.
